sentence: This project builds a map of fetal lung cells from existing data to predict where they come from in childhood lung disease.
This project runs a shared imaging service that prepares tissues and images cells for vision researchers.
This project studies how proteins that let lipids cross membranes work and what they do in cells.
This project studies how chemicals from cannabis in the body predict recovery of thinking and behavior, by sex, in young adults who stop using it.
This project studies how blood proteins and cells change when blood flows through mechanical pumps, and how to lower bleeding or blood clots.
This project studies how proteins that bind RNA clump together as cells age and how this affects cells and lifespan.
This project builds statistical methods to study how genes and the environment in communities together affect many diseases.
This project improves genetic testing tools so they can find disease-linked variants in repeat regions of the genome.
This project builds and tests an imaging tool that uses DNA-based potassium reporters to map voltage activity in small animals without invasive steps.
This project uses light-controlled regulators and small molecules that block aldehyde dehydrogenases to study development and the start of cancer.
This project builds statistical and computational methods to study how nonsense-mediated mRNA decay is controlled in cancers.
This project studies how the adult brain hears and adjusts after gene therapy in the inner ear of deaf mice.
This project tries to find and describe T cells that attack tumors in people with lung cancer.
This project studies why facial wounds heal with less scarring than wounds on the back and abdominal area.
This project studies how purinergic signaling controls blood flow in the brain and supports thinking skills.
This project tests how gene changes and chemical probes affect the structure and network activity of mouse neurons.
This project studies how acetylation changes T cell receptor signaling, using mice and human T cells from melanoma and lung cancer patients.
This project studies how pain affects alcohol drinking in heavy drinkers with and without chronic temporomandibular disorder pain.
